Show your VTuber avatar in OBS

Send a PSD or VRM avatar from V Lens to OBS Studio. Add V Lens Camera, use chroma key, or preserve transparency with Spout2.

The app interface is currently in Japanese. The instructions below include the Japanese menu and control labels.

Add V Lens Camera to OBS

  1. Open a PSD, VRM or built-in sample in V Lens. Set the output destination to Virtual camera (仮想カメラ) and click Start output (出力を開始).
  2. In OBS Studio, add a Video Capture Device in Sources and select V Lens Camera from the device list.
  3. Once the video appears, adjust its size and position in the scene. Configure the microphone for your stream separately in OBS.

If your OBS source used “VCam” in version 0.1.39 or earlier, select “V Lens Camera” again after updating.

Use chroma key or transparent output

For virtual camera output, set Background (背景) to green or blue in V Lens. Add a Chroma Key filter to the video source in OBS and choose the same key color.

To preserve partial transparency, install a compatible Spout2 plugin for OBS and set the output destination in V Lens to Spout2 (transparent) (Spout2（透過）). Add Spout2 Capture in OBS and choose V Lens as the sender. Run OBS with Direct3D 11 and use the same GPU as V Lens.

Download the Spout2 plugin for OBS

If V Lens Camera is missing from the device list

Wait until V Lens shows Output running (出力中), then reopen the device list in OBS. If the virtual camera is not registered, run the Windows installer and approve the virtual camera registration.
